audit.why: Chart already matches the packet exactly (Swain, Skill, Skill, Gwen, Gwen, Gwen, Gwen) and the mirror realigned to the same shape. Level 1 is genuinely yours before she has E or W; everything from 4-5 onward is hers.
Spike placement is right — your level 1, her level 6, her first item, her late game — but spikes[1] and spikes[3] described the wrong mechanics inside the right timings.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three claims are wrong and two of them are repeated. Needlework is called a second dash / engagement tool; Demonic Ascension is said to heal magic damage but not true damage; and Gwen's percent-health damage is attributed to her Q's true damage.
audit.why: Needlework hurls a needle up to 1200 range that slows and can be recast twice — no dash anywhere in it; her only dash is Skip 'n Slash. Swain's drain takes health from nearby enemies and is not conditioned on the damage type he is receiving, so 'it cannot heal true damage' is invented. The real interaction is Hallowed Mist: she can only be targeted by enemies inside it, so a Swain draining from outside has no champion to drain and the form, which lasts only while draining champions, ends. And the health-scaling damage is A Thousand Cuts (magic, and it heals her); Q's true damage applies only to units in the centre of the cone.
audit.corrected: Needlework named as a recastable ranged needle; the mist reframed as ending your drain by removing the target; the health-scaling damage credited to the passive, with Grievous Wounds as the answer.

audit.whatIsWrong: mid tells you to trade when mist is on 'its 16-second cooldown'.
audit.why: Hallowed Mist is 22/21/20/19/18 seconds. Sixteen is not a rank it ever has, and the window you are being told to count is longer than advertised in your favour.

audit.whatIsWrong: Anti-heal appears only as boilerplate in the itemization line.
audit.why: A Thousand Cuts heals her for a portion of the health-scaling damage she deals to champions, which is exactly why your max-HP stacking backfires — Grievous Wounds is not optional here.

edits.before: This is the stretch where the lane tips against you. Gwen's Q true damage does not care that you have been stacking max HP — it percentages right through it — and her Hallowed Mist duration at rank 3-4 is long enough to cover most of your W travel time. At Level 6 you can R to drain and collect fragments, but she can simply W mist and sit inside it, cancelling the heal-for-heal war she would lose. Force trades ONLY when mist is on its 16-second cooldown: W her the instant the mist expires, then E-root if she steps up, then R if she commits. Never open R while she has mist available — she will walk into it, you drain nothing, and her Q true damage still ticks.
edits.after: This is where the lane tips. A Thousand Cuts scales with your health and heals her back, so the max HP you stacked is her resource, and Q adds true damage to anything in the centre of the cone. At Level 6 you can R to drain and collect fragments, but she mists and sits inside: nothing outside the mist can target her, so the drain finds no champion and the form ends on its own. Force trades ONLY on the mist cooldown — 22 seconds at rank 1: W her the instant it expires, throw E so the return pass roots her step-up, then R if she commits. Never open R while mist is available; you drain nothing and pay 120 seconds for it.

edits.before: Gwen's first item is the wall. Nashor's Tooth or Riftmaker turns her Q into a percent-HP true-damage eraser and her already long Hallowed Mist duration covers almost every fight. Your R sustain heals magic damage — it cannot heal true damage — so every second you drain inside her mist she is shredding health you cannot recover. Play the map: rotate to fights where your R drain can hit multiple people (her mist does not protect her there), shove and roam rather than duel her in lane, and build MR to at least require her to commit full items before she deletes you. A direct 1v1 at 2+ items is a loss you should simply decline.
edits.after: Gwen's first item is the wall. Nashor's Tooth or Riftmaker turns her health-scaling passive into an eraser that heals her as it burns you, and her mist covers almost every fight she chooses. The drain is not the answer to it: from outside the mist she cannot be targeted at all, so your ultimate expires with nothing to feed on and 120 seconds gone. Play the map instead — rotate to fights where the drain reaches several bodies at once, shove and roam rather than duel, carry Grievous Wounds, and build MR so she must finish items to delete you. A straight 1v1 at 2+ items is a loss you should decline.

edits.before: Use E dash to close gap and stack Q true-damage autos on your banked Soul Fragment HP
edits.after: Skip 'n Slash in and let A Thousand Cuts turn your banked max HP into her own healing

notes: The damaging error here was a fabricated rule stated twice: that Demonic Ascension 'heals magic damage but cannot heal true damage'. Riot's text has the drain taking health from nearby enemies with no clause about incoming damage types, so the page invented a mechanic and then built the whole late-game section on it. The genuine reason your ultimate fails against Gwen is Hallowed Mist — she can only be targeted from inside it, and the form lasts only while draining champions, so it ends by itself. Needlework was called a dash and a second engagement tool in two places; it is a recastable 1200-range needle, and her only dash is Skip 'n Slash. The percent-health damage was credited to Q's true damage; it is A Thousand Cuts, it is magic, and it heals her — which is what actually makes Grievous Wounds and your fragment stacking interact. Mist cooldown corrected from an invented 16s to 22s at rank 1. Chart already matched the packet, so no chart edits.
